quickAnswerTitle: Tennessee School Calendars Are Set Locally
quickAnswer: Tennessee does not publish one statewide K–12 attendance calendar. State law establishes the school-term framework, while local school boards publish the dates families follow. A featured comparison shows Memphis-Shelby students beginning August 3, Knox County students beginning August 10, and Metro Nashville students beginning August 11. Their main Spring Break weeks fall in different parts of March.
about:
Tennessee's school-term requirements do not create a common first day, Fall Break, Spring Break, or last day for every public school. Local boards publish district calendars within the state framework, and those calendars may use accumulated instructional time, abbreviated days, staff-development dates, and local weather procedures differently. Families therefore need the calendar for their assigned district and, when applicable, their school or program.

A featured comparison uses Metro Nashville Public Schools, Memphis-Shelby County Schools, and Knox County Schools. Their first student dates span August 3–11, and their final student dates span May 20–26. The differences are larger than a one-week opening window suggests: Knox County begins Spring Break March 8, Memphis-Shelby's main Spring Break begins March 15, and Metro Nashville's student closure begins March 22.

The district pages retain details a statewide list would erase. MNPS separates high-school exam half days from districtwide half days and publishes its calendar in seven languages. MSCS distinguishes its Student, Teacher, and Attendance and Report Card Periods calendars, including evening parent conferences that are not automatic no-school days. Knox County starts and ends on half days, schedules additional student half days, and explains how accumulated instructional time contributes to its printed 180-day total.
calendarRulesDescription: Tennessee establishes the school-term and instructional-time framework, but local boards publish the attendance dates, staff days, closures, and weather plans families use.

calendarRules.label: No statewide student calendar
calendarRules.description: Tennessee does not set one first day, break schedule, or last day for every district. Local boards publish the annual calendars used by their schools.

calendarRules.label: The statutory framework includes 180 classroom days
calendarRules.description: Tennessee Code § 49-6-3004 describes a school term of at least 200 days, including 180 days for classroom instruction, five in-service days, one teacher-parent conference day, vacation days, and other locally designated days.

calendarRules.label: A standard grades 1–12 day is at least 6½ hours
calendarRules.description: State attendance guidance treats a shorter grades 1–12 day as abbreviated and allows only a limited number of abbreviated instructional days. Kindergarten and some pre-K programs use different minimum-time rules.

calendarRules.label: Accumulated time can affect printed day counts
calendarRules.description: Tennessee law allows qualifying daily instructional time beyond the minimum to be accumulated for specified uses. A district's printed student-attendance count therefore needs to be read together with its stockpiled or accumulated-time notes.

calendarRules.label: Weather responses remain district-specific
calendarRules.description: Districts publish their own closure, notification, stockpiled-time, make-up, and remote or hybrid-learning procedures. An imported calendar does not update automatically after a weather decision.

stateSections.label: Different Winter Break Labels, the Same January 5 Return
stateSections.content: The calendars in this comparison list Tuesday, January 5, 2027 as the student return date, but they reach it differently. MSCS includes January 4 in Winter Break. MNPS ends its student break December 31, then lists New Year's Day and a January 4 stockpiled professional-development day. Knox County ends Winter Break January 1 and uses January 4 for systemwide in-service and administrative work. The return date matches; the official event labels do not.

stateSections.label: Tennessee Spring Break Dates Vary by District
stateSections.content: The calendars in this comparison place their main Spring Breaks in consecutive weeks: Knox County on March 8–12, Memphis-Shelby on March 15–19, and Metro Nashville on March 22–25 followed by a separate Spring Holiday March 26. MSCS also lists Spring Break II dates later in March. A statewide Spring Break date would therefore be misleading even within this featured comparison.

faqs.q: Does Tennessee have one statewide public school calendar?
faqs.a: No. Tennessee establishes school-term and instructional-time requirements, but local school boards publish their own attendance calendars. First days, breaks, staff dates, half days, weather responses, and last days vary by district and sometimes by grade or program.

faqs.q: When do Tennessee schools start in 2026?
faqs.a: There is no single statewide start date. In the reviewed 2026–27 collection, Memphis-Shelby students begin August 3, Knox County students begin August 10, and Metro Nashville students begin August 11. Other Tennessee districts may use different dates.

faqs.q: How many instructional days are required in Tennessee public schools?
faqs.a: Tennessee's school-term framework includes 180 days for classroom instruction. District calendars may also explain accumulated instructional time, abbreviated days, in-service days, parent conferences, and weather provisions, so a raw count of visible student dates may not tell the full story.

faqs.q: Do Tennessee districts have the same Spring Break?
faqs.a: No. The featured comparison uses different main Spring Break weeks: Knox County lists March 8–12, Memphis-Shelby lists March 15–19, and Metro Nashville lists March 22–25 followed by a separate Spring Holiday on March 26.

faqs.q: When do the reviewed Tennessee districts return after Winter Break?
faqs.a: Metro Nashville, Memphis-Shelby, and Knox County students all return Tuesday, January 5, 2027. Their official calendars describe the preceding days differently, so use the district page for the complete break, holiday, and staff-day sequence.

faqs.q: Can I add a Tennessee school calendar to Google Calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. The reviewed Tennessee district pages provide ICS files for Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook. Each file is a one-time import and will not automatically reflect later district revisions, school-specific events, or weather changes.

footerNote: Tennessee calendar dates are sourced from official state guidance and district-published calendars. Districts may revise calendars after publication, so confirm current dates with the assigned district before making fixed plans.
